transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-16
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Evan (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood CSM), Priya (Argent Eng Mgr), Jorge (Argent Infra), Nina (Argent Security), Tom (Argent SRE), Leah (Argent Product)

---
Summary (auto):
Redwood walked through the incident timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations applied during the incident, and long-term fixes. Customer asked for details on patch timing, audit logs, and options around Dedicated/VPC for isolation. Call ended with agreement on next steps and concrete action owners.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. quick recaps, this is the postmortem follow up from the 8/12 latency event. Evan and I will run through timeline then go to q and a.
[00:22] Priya: thanks Maya, yeah we had multiple app teams flagging timeouts, looked pretty bad on our side, want to understand root cause and what you patched.
[00:34] Evan: yeah i'll take first pass — timeline we saw an autoscaler decision flip around 14:17 UTC where the pool scaled down one GPU node while a set of long-context requests were still hot, that triggered a KV cache invalidation and rewarm. the rewarm plus model fallbacks caused token generation queuing and then request timeouts.
[01:05] Tom: just to be clear — requests weren't dropped en masse, they were queued and we hit our client-side 25s timeout for some endpoints.
[01:18] Jorge: we also saw an unusual spike in concurrent connections at the time; could be traffic burst from a batch job. i can share our cron jobs in that window.
[01:30] Evan: thanks, that helps. the autoscaler we use has a race condition in the drain path — when nodes are terminated the runtime sometimes invalidates KV prefixes prematurely, that plus an aggressive batching policy meant rewarm was expensive. also there was an alert threshold misconfiguration so SLO alerting didn't escalate immediately.
[02:05] Nina: from security's standpoint were any logs or PII affected? we need to know for our audit and SOC2 evidence.
[02:18] Maya: quick answer — no data exfiltration, but some request traces were truncated in the short window. we'll provide the audit logs and the chain of custody notes. Evan can describe what logs we have.
[02:36] Evan: we retained runtime metrics, kernel traces, and partial KV cache state snapshots for the window. i'll bundle those and the timeline. note: some of the auto-transcribed names might look odd — the runtime call traces reference 'K V cache' in places due to tokenizer; sorry for noise.
[03:02] Leah: what's the immediate fix you pushed? did we roll back something?
[03:12] Maya: yes — at 14:28 we applied a hotfix: tightened the autoscaler cooldown and disabled the aggressive batch merging for the affected model family. that reduced rewarm cost and throughput normalized by 14:45. we also reverted a recent scheduling tweak that had lowered the grace period.
[03:40] Priya: did that involve a restart? any risk of lost state?
[03:46] Evan: no full restart, we used a graceful drain + patch, there was some cache recompute but no persisted state loss.
[03:56] Tom: can you explain more about the cache invalidation? our team sees 'KV cache invalidation' in the logs but want deeper detail — was it prefix eviction or whole-shard?
[04:08] Evan: good q. it looked like a prefix eviction triggered by the drain handler; under load the handler's logic considered prefixes stale and evicted them which forced full sequence recomputation when requests resumed. whole-shard eviction wasn't observed, but prefix churn was enough to cause rewarm overhead.
[04:40] Jorge: will you be changing eviction policy?
[04:44] Evan: yes — immediate mitigation is to add a conservative cooldown on eviction during scale-downs and to delay prefix eviction until we've confirmed no active long-context sessions. longer-term we plan to add circuit breakers so model fallback and evictions don't cascade into SLO violations.
[05:10] Maya: one more note: we added a temporary rule to route critical endpoints to a pinned model variant that doesn't use the aggressive batching kernel while we validate.
[05:25] Priya: ok, that explains the temporary latency but why did alerts not fire?
[05:30] Lena: that was on us — alert thresholds for queue depth were set after the last tuning; during the burst queue depth increased but didn't cross the older threshold. we will push an alert config update and add a runbook for scaling anomalies.
[05:58] Nina: for compliance, Argent needs complete audit logs for the incident window, plus a statement about whether any encrypted data keys were exposed.
[06:12] Maya: we do not have evidence of key material exposure; data at rest and in transit remained encrypted. we'll provide KMS access logs and HSM attestations where applicable.
[06:30] Nina: OK please add that to the postmortem.
[06:36] Evan: technical follow-ups — I'm going to propose three workstreams: 1) autoscaler fix (code patch + safer drain), 2) runtime resilience (circuit breaker for fallback and cache eviction), 3) observability (alert thresholds, tracing retention), plus a controlled canary rollout for the fixes.
[06:58] Jorge: rough ETA on the autoscaler fix?
[07:02] Evan: patch is ready for internal review, we can release to staging in 3 business days and to prod with a canary in 7-10 days pending tests.
[07:14] Priya: can Argent help with the staging tests? we can run traffic patterns that mimic the batch jobs.
[07:20] Maya: absolutely — we'll coordinate a test plan. Evan will own the test harness and Jorge/Tom will provide traffic replay.
[07:31] Tom: remember to include our timeouts; we may need to extend some client-side timeouts while caches rewarm during the canary.
[07:40] Evan: noted. for longer-term reliability improvements, we suggested: tunable batch sizing per route, model quantization profiles for faster rewarm, and prefix-sticky cache allocation.
[07:58] Leah: on the Dedicated idea — Leah here — we want to understand the isolation benefits vs the hosted approach; could Dedicated avoid these kinds of cross-tenant scaling races?
[08:12] Maya: Dedicated helps because you control capacity and autoscaling policies at a reservation level; fewer noisy neighbors. that said, autoscaler bugs can still affect a single tenant if config is aggressive. Dedicated plus pinned capacity and conservative autoscaling would reduce risk.
[08:30] Leah: pricing and timeline?
[08:33] Maya: we'll send a Dedicated pilot proposal — baseline sizing, cost estimate, and timeline. pilot could be 4-6 weeks to validate.
[08:42] Priya: security review for Dedicated — will we still get audit logs and KMS integration?
[08:47] Maya: yes, Dedicated includes VPC options, KMS/HSM integrations, and longer audit log retention as add-ons. Evan: we can show the integration diagram.
[09:00] Nina: we need sample SOC2 artifacts for your hosting model, and details on RBAC/SSO.
[09:06] Lena: we'll package SOC2 summary, SSO/SAML docs, RBAC examples, and recent pen test summary.
[09:16] Priya: what about automatic fallbacks to smaller models — that sometimes reduces latency but can affect quality and cause retries.
[09:25] Evan: right — we now have a policy engine that chooses fallback based on cost/latency tiers; we'll add a quality gate so we don't fallback below a defined quality threshold for critical routes.
[09:40] Tom: are we tracking model version pinning? some of our endpoints expect deterministic outputs.
[09:45] Maya: yes, you can pin model versions and we support rollbacks/rollouts with canary traffic. we'll include instructions in the postmortem.
[09:55] Priya: i want to call out customer impact — we had ~120 failed requests across three endpoints, mostly timeouts, a handful of slower responses. some users saw multi-second latency increases.
[10:12] Maya: thanks for that. we will include the user impact and estimated SLA credit in the postmortem.
[10:20] Leah: what's the plan for long-term regression prevention?
[10:24] Evan: add canaries, synthetic health checks for long-context sessions, and an autoscaler simulation tool we can run against customer configs. also improve tracing to correlate KV cache churn with autoscaler events.
[10:45] Jorge: that simulation tool would be very helpful — we can run it against our infra prior to deployments.
[10:52] Evan: we'll get you access to the simulator and a sample runbook.
[11:00] Maya: ok wrapping up, can we confirm action owners? Evan will share logs and traces, Maya will send postmortem + credit proposal, Jorge will share cluster events, Nina will list security artifacts.
[11:18] Priya: yes all good. also can we schedule the infra deep-dive next week?
[11:22] Maya: tentatively Thursday 2027-08-19 16:00 UTC; i'll send invite after checking availability.
[11:30] Tom: quick q — will this patch affect latency for cold starts?
[11:34] Evan: ideally reduces cold-start penalty by avoiding full prefix eviction; there may be slight overhead from delayed eviction windows but net effect is improved stability.
[11:46] Nina: thanks everyone, please include the security checklist in the postmortem.
[11:50] Maya: will do. thanks all for the time.
